solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Maybe money that's left on account, last of salary

indicators.note: last of points to the closing letter of the following word only

blocks.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
AC is the usual abbreviation for account
the final letter of salary

explanation.surface: Someone describes an inheritance left in a bank account, topped up by the end of a pay packet.
explanation.walkthrough: The on side in cricket (the half of the field behind the batter's legs) is the leg side, a regular crossword equivalence.
explanation.definitionFit: A legacy is a bequest, typically money left to someone in a will; 'Maybe' marks money as only one example.

clue.text: Lady Fortune, according to Spooner, is a weakling

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner was famous for swapping the first sounds of neighbouring words

blocks.note: a dame is a titled lady and luck is fortune

explanation.surface: Lady Luck herself is cast as feeble, as if Fortune had become a pushover.
explanation.definitionFit: A lame duck is an idiom for a person or thing that is ineffectual or in difficulties, so a weakling.

clue.text: Vocalist crooned with head down amid grand cheers

indicators.note: in a down entry the first letter is moved to the bottom, the end of the word
amid means in the middle of, so this word sits between the other two

blocks.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
to croon is to sing softly
ta is British slang for thanks

explanation.surface: A crooner takes a bow, head lowered, amid loud applause.
explanation.walkthrough: Ta is British for thank you, which crosswords use for cheers.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangsta is a rapper in the gangsta rap style, so a kind of vocalist; the clue's croon scene hides a rough genre.

clue.text: Succeed using computers? Pull the other one!

blocks.note: a plan that comes off succeeds
IT is information technology, the world of computers

explanation.surface: A sceptic mocks the claim that computers bring success.
explanation.walkthrough: Pull the other one (it's got bells on) is a British retort meaning I don't believe you.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are colloquial exclamations of disbelief telling the speaker to stop pretending or exaggerating.

clue.text: Person acquiring a record: disc with loud guitar

blocks.note: the letter O is disc-shaped
f is forte, loud in music
Fender is a famous make of electric guitar

explanation.surface: A record collector buys a disc and a loud electric guitar.
explanation.walkthrough: Record misleads: not vinyl but a criminal record.
explanation.definitionFit: An offender is someone who commits a crime and so gains a criminal record.

clue.text: During sunny day, scoff that lady's underwear is silly

indicators.note: during places the following words within the span of the preceding ones

blocks.note: fine weather is sunny weather
D is the abbreviation for day
to scoff is to eat greedily
her is the possessive of she, that lady
a bra is an item of underwear

explanation.surface: On a sunny day someone gobbles down a woman's lingerie, which is plainly daft.
explanation.walkthrough: Sunny day splits around the middle: the scoffing and the lady's underwear sit between its first letter and the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Featherbrained describes someone with a head as light as feathers, so foolish or silly.

clue.text: Dismiss half of costs on line

indicators.note: only half the word is kept, so its second half is dropped

blocks.note: expenses are costs
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A boss sacks someone over half the costs on a production line.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel is to dismiss or throw out, as a school expels a pupil.

clue.text: Write quickly — from France's capital

indicators.note: a capital here is the leading letter, the head of the word

blocks.note: the punctuation mark itself is a dash
of can mean from, as in a man of Kent
the capital letter of France

explanation.surface: A note is dashed off in a hurry, sent from the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash is not punctuation for the surface but part of the wordplay; capital means first letter, not Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash off a letter is an idiom for writing it hurriedly.

clue.text: Painter's frames for rococo triptych a stunning hit

indicators.note: a frame is the edge of a picture, so only the edge letters of each word count

blocks.note: the first and last letters of rococo
the first and last letters of triptych
a KO is a knockout, a blow that stuns

explanation.surface: A painter puts frames round a rococo triptych and it is a smash.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for is; Mark Rothko was the American abstract painter of colour-field canvases.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Rothko was a celebrated twentieth-century American painter, so the surname names a painter.

clue.text: A compiler into version of Handel American musicians play

indicators.note: into means the first pair of words goes inside the composer's name
a version is a rendering in another form, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
the compiler of a crossword refers to themselves as I
taken as written
US is short for American
a band is a group of musicians

explanation.surface: A setter joins an American band playing an arrangement of Handel.
explanation.walkthrough: Play is the definition, not an instruction to the musicians; the compiler is the setter, I.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ideal Husband is a comic play by Oscar Wilde, first staged in 1895.

clue.text: Obsession of Arab, blocking title given to Lisa

indicators.note: something blocking a passage sits inside it

blocks.note: the Mona Lisa is Leonardo's portrait
an Omani is an Arab from Oman

explanation.surface: An Arab is fixated on the Mona Lisa, blocking her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Monomania is an obsession with a single subject or idea.

clue.text: Assume German cheers after eliminating resistance

indicators.note: eliminating means removing, so that letter is struck out

blocks.note: prosit is a German drinking toast
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone assumes Germans cheer once the resistance has been crushed.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward as a premise, so to assume something for argument.

clue.text: Kind of pop record's sleeve showing lack of harmony

indicators.note: a sleeve wraps round a record, so only the outside letters are kept

blocks.note: disco is a style of pop music
the first and last letters of record

explanation.surface: A disco record's cover reveals a band that cannot agree.
explanation.definitionFit: Discord means disagreement or, in music, a clash of notes, the opposite of harmony.

clue.text: Minor eminence not well dressed in white

indicators.note: something dressed in clothing is wrapped by it

blocks.note: hock is a German white wine
ill means not well

explanation.surface: A lesser dignitary, feeling unwell, is dressed in white robes.
explanation.walkthrough: Eminence suggests a cardinal; here it is a raised piece of ground. Hock is a British name for Rhine wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A hillock is a small hill, and an eminence is a piece of rising ground.

clue.text: Banter with pair of females after a drink

indicators.note: after says the female pair follows on behind the drink

blocks.note: cha is slang for tea
F for female, twice

explanation.surface: Two women chat and joke over a cup of something.
explanation.walkthrough: Cha (or char) is British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaff is light-hearted teasing talk, the same as banter.

clue.text: E.g. fighter's great skill, boxing right

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, as a box holds its contents

blocks.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI in crosswords
R is short for right
craft is skill

explanation.surface: A boxer's great skill shows in fighting with the right hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Fighter suggests a boxer, but it is a fighter plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A fighter plane is one type of aircraft, hence the 'E.g.'.

clue.text: One possibly barking puzzle supplier for the Morning Star?

blocks.note: the Morning Star is a British communist newspaper, and a communist is a red
a setter supplies crossword puzzles

explanation.surface: Someone wonders who sets the crossword for the Morning Star, perhaps a crank.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking, British for mad, points at the puzzle setter; it is a dog barking.
explanation.definitionFit: A red setter is a breed of gun dog, and a dog is a creature that barks.

clue.text: Oddly keen to block friendly state, one involved in assembly

indicators.note: oddly means strangely, so the letters come out in a peculiar order
to block something is to sit inside it as an obstruction

blocks.note: an ally is a friendly nation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A keen rival tries to frustrate a friendly state engaged in some assembly.
explanation.walkthrough: Oddly looks like it takes odd letters; here it shuffles all four.
explanation.definitionFit: An Allen key is the hexagonal tool used for flat-pack furniture assembly.

clue.text: Will one carp see inside boat? I'm not sure

definitions.note: read as a question: a person who will carp

indicators.note: inside places the first item within the next

blocks.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat
v is vide, Latin for see
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: An angler wonders whether a carp will be seen inside the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Carp is the verb to complain, not the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Kvetch is Yiddish-derived slang for complaining, so a kvetcher is a habitual carper.

clue.text: See a deer and beat it

blocks.note: v is vide, Latin for see
taken as written
a moose is a large deer

explanation.surface: Spotting a large deer, you run for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Vamoose is slang for leave quickly, the same as the idiom beat it.

clue.text: Lodge in valley accommodating wife

indicators.note: accommodating means housing, holding something within

blocks.note: a dell is a small wooded valley
W is short for wife

explanation.surface: A couple take lodgings in a valley house that has room for the wife.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge is to live somewhere, and to dwell means to reside.

clue.text: Night before receiving a signal, one gets rescued

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, holding the next words inside

blocks.note: an eve is the night before an event
taken as written
a cue is a signal to act

explanation.surface: The night before, a signal comes through and someone is saved.
explanation.walkthrough: Wartime British children sent to the country were evacuees.
explanation.definitionFit: An evacuee is a person removed from danger, so one who is rescued.

clue.text: Play heroine part and heartless Iago amazingly

indicators.note: without a heart, so the two middle letters are taken out
something amazing defies the ordinary, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean heroine plays her role opposite a villainous Iago, to astonishing effect.
explanation.walkthrough: Iago is the villain of Othello, but Portia is the heroine of The Merchant of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: Portia is the heroine of Shakespeare's play The Merchant of Venice.

clue.text: East Germans taking very little time in assimilation

indicators.note: taking means taking in, holding inside

blocks.note: Ossis is German slang for former East Germans
a mo is a moment

explanation.surface: East Germans were absorbed into the West in hardly any time.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmosis is gradual absorption of ideas or a fluid, a figurative assimilation.

clue.text: American soldiers in retreat showing character

indicators.note: a retreating army goes back the way it came

blocks.note: Am is short for American
GIs are US soldiers

explanation.surface: US troops in retreat show what they are made of.
explanation.walkthrough: Character means a letter, here of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigma is the eighteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a character.

clue.text: Once again, go over most of renegotiated treaties

indicators.note: most of means all but the final letter
a renegotiated deal has its terms rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Diplomats revisit most of a set of treaties they had already reworked.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to repeat or perform again, going over something once more.

clue.text: Ruffian, working for university, is one showing a lot of cheek?

definitions.text: one showing a lot of cheek?

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one thing replaces another

blocks.note: a thug is a ruffian
a machine that is on is working
U is short for university

explanation.surface: A hooligan swaps university for a job and becomes very cheeky.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheek here is the buttock, not impudence; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is skimpy underwear or swimwear that leaves the buttocks largely bare.

clue.text: Staggered towards the sunset in a crowd

indicators.note: in places this direction inside the crowd phrase

blocks.note: a ruck is a crowd or throng
the sun sets in the west

explanation.surface: Someone staggers off into the sunset among a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Staggered looks like reeling about; it means astonished.
explanation.definitionFit: To be staggered is to be astounded, and awestruck means overwhelmed with wonder.

clue.text: Supply deal secured by helper making capital

indicators.note: supply read as supple-ly, flexibly bent into a new shape
something secured by another is held within it

blocks.note: an aide is an assistant
taken as written

explanation.surface: An assistant secures a supply contract that brings in money.
explanation.walkthrough: Supply reads as a verb but is the adverb from supple, a flexible-looking anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Adelaide is the capital city of the state of South Australia.

clue.text: Cook fish slices in great quantities

indicators.note: a slicing knife goes into the thing it cuts

blocks.note: to fry is to cook
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A cook slices up fish in large amounts.
explanation.walkthrough: Slices reads as a noun of fish slices; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Freely can mean abundantly or without stint, so given in great quantities.
